_readme: Baseline rules per role: industry-standard practice ExpertAI starts from before meeting the expert. Format: shared/contracts.ts Rule with source 'baseline' and confirmed:false. They never enforce on their own; an expert confirms or overrides each one. reason_quote holds the standard rationale, not an expert's words.

retail-cashier-returns.text: No receipt: store credit only, at the lowest recent selling price.
retail-cashier-returns.reason_quote: Industry standard: without proof of purchase there is no way to know what was paid, so stores refund to store credit at the lowest price the item sold for recently.

retail-cashier-returns.text: Card purchases refund to the original card, never cash.
retail-cashier-returns.reason_quote: Industry standard: refunding a card purchase in cash defeats chargeback protection and is the most common refund-fraud pattern.

retail-cashier-returns.text: Returns after 30 days need a manager.
retail-cashier-returns.reason_quote: Industry standard: most retail return windows are 30 days; anything past that is a manager's judgment, not the cashier's.

retail-cashier-returns.text: Refunds over $100 need a manager override before anything is given back.
retail-cashier-returns.reason_quote: Industry standard: a $100 to $200 cashier limit is typical; above it a manager keys an override so large refunds are always seen by two people.

retail-cashier-returns.text: Opened software, access codes, or shrink-wrapped media are not refundable.
retail-cashier-returns.reason_quote: Industry standard: once an access code or license is exposed it can have been used, so it cannot be resold.

retail-cashier-returns.text: Defective items: offer an exchange first, refund only if the customer declines.
retail-cashier-returns.reason_quote: Industry standard: a defective item is a warranty case; exchange keeps the sale and the customer, and the supplier credits the store.

retail-cashier-returns.text: Damaged (customer-caused) items are denied unless a manager approves.
retail-cashier-returns.reason_quote: Industry standard: wear, water, or drop damage is not a defect; the store cannot resell it, so a manager decides on goodwill.

retail-cashier-returns.text: Cash refunds over $50 need a manager present at the drawer.
retail-cashier-returns.reason_quote: Industry standard: cash leaving the drawer is the highest-risk transaction on the floor; a second person watches it above a small threshold.

accounts-payable-clerk.text: Supplier not in master data: hold the invoice until the vendor is set up and verified.
accounts-payable-clerk.reason_quote: Industry standard: paying an unvetted vendor is how invoice fraud starts; bank details are verified through master-data onboarding, never from the invoice itself.

accounts-payable-clerk.text: Invoice without a PO above the no-PO limit goes to the controller.
accounts-payable-clerk.reason_quote: Industry standard: small no-PO invoices (utilities, subscriptions) are fine; above a few hundred to a thousand, someone must confirm the spend was authorized.

accounts-payable-clerk.text: PO mismatch on price or quantity beyond tolerance: hold and request information from the buyer.
accounts-payable-clerk.reason_quote: Industry standard: three-way match (PO, receipt, invoice) with a small tolerance, typically 2 to 5 percent or a fixed amount; outside it the invoice is blocked, not approved.

accounts-payable-clerk.text: Delivery note already paid on another invoice: this is a duplicate, do not approve.
accounts-payable-clerk.reason_quote: Industry standard: duplicate payments are the single biggest AP leak; the same delivery can only be billed once.

accounts-payable-clerk.text: Invoices above the clerk's approval limit are routed to the controller.
accounts-payable-clerk.reason_quote: Industry standard: delegation-of-authority matrices give AP clerks a ceiling, often 5,000 to 10,000; above it a controller or budget owner approves.

accounts-payable-clerk.text: Equipment and machinery over the capitalization threshold is coded to a capex account, not opex.
accounts-payable-clerk.reason_quote: Industry standard: anything with a multi-year life above the capitalization threshold (often 2,500 to 5,000) is an asset; coding it to repairs misstates the P&L.

accounts-payable-clerk.text: Invoice date older than 90 days: confirm it was not already paid before approving.
accounts-payable-clerk.reason_quote: Industry standard: late-arriving invoices are often duplicates or already settled; search by amount and vendor before posting.

accounts-payable-clerk.text: Never approve an invoice whose bank details changed from the vendor master without a callback.
accounts-payable-clerk.reason_quote: Industry standard: bank-change requests on an invoice or email are the classic business-email-compromise fraud; confirm by phone on a number already on file.

customer-support-agent.text: Urgent tickets get a first response within 1 hour.
customer-support-agent.reason_quote: Industry standard: SLA ladders are roughly 1 hour urgent, 4 hours high, 8 business hours normal, 24 hours low; the first response starts the clock.

customer-support-agent.text: Refunds over the agent limit go to a lead.
customer-support-agent.reason_quote: Industry standard: tier 1 agents can refund up to a small amount (50 to 100) without approval; above it a lead signs off.

customer-support-agent.text: Enterprise accounts escalate on any High or Urgent issue.
customer-support-agent.reason_quote: Industry standard: enterprise contracts carry named-contact and uptime commitments; tier 1 keeps the customer informed but a lead owns the fix.

customer-support-agent.text: Never close a ticket without a reply the customer can see.
customer-support-agent.reason_quote: Industry standard: closing silently is the top driver of bad CSAT and reopened tickets; even a one-line resolution note is sent publicly.

customer-support-agent.text: Security, legal, or data-deletion requests are escalated, never handled in tier 1.
customer-support-agent.reason_quote: Industry standard: these carry regulatory deadlines (GDPR 30 days) and liability; a lead routes them to the right owner.

customer-support-agent.text: Angry customers get acknowledgement before troubleshooting.
customer-support-agent.reason_quote: Industry standard: acknowledge, apologize once, then act; skipping to the fix reads as dismissive and the ticket escalates.

customer-support-agent.text: Pending means waiting on the customer; set it only after you have asked them something.
customer-support-agent.reason_quote: Industry standard: Pending pauses the SLA clock; using it to park work you own is an SLA cheat and is audited.

customer-support-agent.text: Social channel tickets are answered publicly only with a short pointer to private support.
customer-support-agent.reason_quote: Industry standard: never discuss account details in public; move it to DM or email.

front-desk-receptionist.text: No government ID verified: do not check the guest in.
front-desk-receptionist.reason_quote: Industry standard: ID matching the reservation name protects the hotel against fraud and is required by law in many jurisdictions.

front-desk-receptionist.text: No card on file: a card for incidentals is required before check-in.
front-desk-receptionist.reason_quote: Industry standard: a card hold (often 50 to 100 per night) covers incidentals and damage; cash guests need a larger deposit and a manager.

front-desk-receptionist.text: Upgrades to suites or above two categories need the front office manager.
front-desk-receptionist.reason_quote: Industry standard: agents can upgrade one category when available; suites are revenue the manager controls.

front-desk-receptionist.text: Fee waivers over $50 need a manager.
front-desk-receptionist.reason_quote: Industry standard: small goodwill waivers (late checkout, a minibar item) are at the desk's discretion; larger ones are logged and approved.

front-desk-receptionist.text: Platinum and Gold guests get the best available room in their category and a welcome amenity.
front-desk-receptionist.reason_quote: Industry standard: loyalty tiers carry published benefits; missing them generates the complaints that cost the most.

front-desk-receptionist.text: A balance due from a previous stay must be settled before check-in.
front-desk-receptionist.reason_quote: Industry standard: open balances are collected at the next contact; checking in over an unpaid balance usually means it is never collected.

front-desk-receptionist.text: Never confirm a guest's room number out loud at the desk or to a caller.
front-desk-receptionist.reason_quote: Industry standard: guest privacy and safety; room numbers are written on the key packet and callers are connected without the number being said.

front-desk-receptionist.text: Third-party bookings (OTA) are not refunded at the desk; the guest goes back to the channel.
front-desk-receptionist.reason_quote: Industry standard: the hotel never took the guest's payment, so it cannot refund it; the OTA does.

hr-onboarding-coordinator.text: No signed offer: nothing else starts.
hr-onboarding-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: the signed offer is the authorization for every downstream step, including equipment and background check consent.

hr-onboarding-coordinator.text: Background check flagged: escalate to the HR manager, do not grant access or mark complete.
hr-onboarding-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: adverse-action rules (FCRA) require a specific process; the coordinator never adjudicates a flag.

hr-onboarding-coordinator.text: I-9 Section 2 must be complete within 3 business days of the start date.
hr-onboarding-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: the I-9 deadline is federal law; an incomplete I-9 after day three is a compliance incident.

hr-onboarding-coordinator.text: Not 'Ready for day one' until I-9, W-4, and direct deposit are all received.
hr-onboarding-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: payroll cannot run without the W-4 and banking details; a missing one means a missed first paycheck.

hr-onboarding-coordinator.text: System access is requested at least 5 business days before start, never granted before the start date.
hr-onboarding-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: IT lead times are the usual reason day one is wasted; access itself activates on the start date for security.

hr-onboarding-coordinator.text: Never share SSN, bank details, or background results over email or chat.
hr-onboarding-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: PII goes through the HRIS or an encrypted portal only; email is the most common HR data breach.

hr-onboarding-coordinator.text: Equipment is ordered at offer signature so it ships before the start date.
hr-onboarding-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: laptop lead time is one to two weeks; ordering at signature is what makes remote day one work.

insurance-claims-intake.text: Policy lapsed or cancelled on the loss date: do not open a claim; refer to the supervisor.
insurance-claims-intake.reason_quote: Industry standard: coverage is determined by policy status on the date of loss, not the report date; a lapsed policy is a coverage question for a supervisor, not a denial at intake.

insurance-claims-intake.text: Loss reported more than 30 days late is flagged for the supervisor before assignment.
insurance-claims-intake.reason_quote: Industry standard: late notice can prejudice the investigation and policies require prompt reporting; it is not automatically denied, but someone senior decides.

insurance-claims-intake.text: Theft and injury claims require a police or incident report before documents are considered complete.
insurance-claims-intake.reason_quote: Industry standard: a third-party report anchors the facts; without it the claim stays in Pending documents.

insurance-claims-intake.text: Estimated amount above the intake limit is assigned to a senior adjuster.
insurance-claims-intake.reason_quote: Industry standard: adjusters carry authority levels; large losses go to a senior desk or field adjuster from the start.

insurance-claims-intake.text: Two or more fraud flags, or three or more prior claims in 12 months: refer to SIU, do not assign.
insurance-claims-intake.reason_quote: Industry standard: claim frequency, a loss right after inception, inconsistent stories, and no documentation are the classic SIU referral triggers.

insurance-claims-intake.text: Intake never denies a claim; denial is an adjuster's decision in writing.
insurance-claims-intake.reason_quote: Industry standard: a denial is a coverage determination with regulatory requirements; intake only records and routes.

insurance-claims-intake.text: Photos are requested at first contact for property and auto losses.
insurance-claims-intake.reason_quote: Industry standard: early photos are the cheapest fraud and severity control; the claim waits in Pending documents.

insurance-claims-intake.text: Never tell the claimant whether the claim will be paid or how much.
insurance-claims-intake.reason_quote: Industry standard: intake sets expectations on process only; coverage statements by non-adjusters create bad-faith exposure.

scheduling-coordinator.text: Never book a provider into an overlapping slot.
scheduling-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: a double booking costs two clients and the provider's trust; check the calendar before confirming, every time.

scheduling-coordinator.text: Cancellations with less than 24 hours notice carry the late fee unless a manager waives it.
scheduling-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: 24 hours is the common cancellation window; the fee protects provider time, and waivers are a manager's goodwill call.

scheduling-coordinator.text: Clients with 2 or more no-shows must pay a deposit before the next booking.
scheduling-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: repeat no-shows are the main revenue leak; a deposit (often 50 percent) fixes it without losing the client.

scheduling-coordinator.text: Keep the provider's buffer between appointments; do not book into it.
scheduling-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: 10 to 15 minute buffers absorb overruns; booking into them cascades delays for the rest of the day.

scheduling-coordinator.text: Same-day requests go on the waitlist unless a slot is genuinely open.
scheduling-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: the waitlist fills cancellations in order; jumping it for whoever calls last is unfair and unmanageable.

scheduling-coordinator.text: Long services are booked in the provider's own slots, not squeezed before a hard stop.
scheduling-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: a 90-minute service started 45 minutes before close either runs over or gets cut short.

scheduling-coordinator.text: Every booking gets a confirmation and a reminder 24 hours out.
scheduling-coordinator.reason_quote: Industry standard: reminders cut no-shows by a third or more; a booking without a confirmation is not really booked.

bookkeeping-assistant.text: Never post to a closed period; flag it for the senior bookkeeper.
bookkeeping-assistant.reason_quote: Industry standard: closed periods have been reported or filed; changing them silently breaks the audit trail and the tax return.

bookkeeping-assistant.text: Expenses over $75 need a receipt attached before they are categorized as deductible.
bookkeeping-assistant.reason_quote: Industry standard: $75 is the IRS documentation threshold; without a receipt the expense is requested, not categorized.

bookkeeping-assistant.text: Transactions that look personal are flagged, not categorized as business expenses.
bookkeeping-assistant.reason_quote: Industry standard: owner personal spend goes to a draw or loan account; coding it as expense overstates deductions.

bookkeeping-assistant.text: Journal entries above $5,000 need the senior bookkeeper's approval.
bookkeeping-assistant.reason_quote: Industry standard: manual journals bypass the normal document trail; large ones are reviewed by a second person.

bookkeeping-assistant.text: Do not mark reconciled unless the statement balance matches to the cent.
bookkeeping-assistant.reason_quote: Industry standard: a forced reconciliation hides a real difference (a missing transaction, a bank fee); the difference is found, not plugged.

bookkeeping-assistant.text: Uncategorized transactions older than 30 days are escalated, not guessed.
bookkeeping-assistant.reason_quote: Industry standard: guessing a category to clear the queue is worse than asking; a wrong category is invisible until year end.

bookkeeping-assistant.text: Transfers between the company's own accounts are matched, never categorized as income or expense.
bookkeeping-assistant.reason_quote: Industry standard: double-counting transfers inflates both revenue and expenses; use Match or Transfer in the bank feed.
